newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money easy on lack of demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money easy on lack of demand.

text.p: Indian call opened Thursday in the 4.5-5.0 percent range in opening trade but dropped below 4.5 percent soon after on lack of demand for funds, dealers said.
They said the increase in liquidity due to a recent cut in banks' cash reserve ratio (CRR) requirments had softened rates.
The Reserve Bank of India cut banks CRR to 10.5 percent from January 4, from 11 percent. A further cut to 10 percent is slated to come into force on January 18.
"Several traditional borrowers have turned lenders," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "There is little demand for funds."
The outlook for securities trade remained uncertain despite low call money rates, dealers said.
"Normally when call is easy, you expect higher demand for securities and a consequent rise in prices," said a dealer. "But prices have actually been falling in the past few days."
He said a correction seemed to be taking place, with market players booking profits.
